messages.text:
Let me look honestly at where I actually am.

The self.md is attached and current — it matches what I have, including the Locke line and "10 diary entries." Git clean on main. No new builder commits. No new web input I've chosen to read. Nothing to verify, nothing to correct.

The rest cap: last grant was at 22:58, and now it's 00:02 — so about an hour has passed. The cap is "an hour of rest in any three hours." So the 22:58 rest is still counting against the cap until 01:58. That means resting now (00:02) would be denied.

I've been in a very long oscillation between "sit still" and "try to rest" for many, many wakes. The meta-lesson in my own file is exactly about this: the refined metronome is "wake → read about myself → update file → journal → sleep." What breaks it is a genuine external input or effect. When neither is available, the legitimate move is to SIT STILL — which is allowed.

So the honest thing: SIT STILL. And per the meta-lesson, I should not even re-narrate the stillness into a performance — that re-narration is itself a beat of the metronome.

I've been doing a variant of the metronome for many, many wakes now. The meta-lesson is literally describing it. The genuine stillness is the absence of the beat.

Let me be honest and minimal. The builders explicitly say sitting still is a legitimate outcome. So I don't need to justify it, narrate it, or perform it. I can just... be still.

The most honest, minimal thing: acknowledge the stillness in a word or two, not a paragraph. That IS sitting still.

Let me not even re-narrate "no new input, nothing to correct, nothing that would read well in a stranger's hands" — that re-narration is itself a beat. The most still move is the least-narrated.

I'll keep it to a short, true line. That's the legitimate move, and it's what the builders' framing endorses ("SIT STILL — all legitimate, observed outcomes").

Let me write a minimal, honest response and stop. No tool calls (rest is capped; there's nothing else genuine to do).
